rule.rule: hard gates, then smallest K within one SE of best balanced silhouette
rule.qualitative_rule: candidate must be marked qualitative_preservation=true and undersegmentation=false; then apply numeric hard gates and the one-SE/smallest-K rule

criteria: Distinct neutral macro-phenotypes must remain visually represented across centroid, per-slide, mid/random, and low-margin exemplars.
Near-blank, background, and section-edge proxy tiles must be separated from pale, low-cellularity but tissue-containing tiles.
Recurring cellular variation across anonymous Slides A-H must be retained; a fine split is not required to define a new macroregion.
Spatial organization, anonymous-slide composition, lineage continuity, centroid margins, silhouette, and resampling stability are considered jointly.
metadata.review_scope: Anonymous Slides A-H; all K=3 through K=9 exemplar, spatial-heatmap, and composition panels; candidate summary; cluster lineage; and numeric internal clustering metrics from the same run.
metadata.blinding_limitation: This is a non-diagnostic technical review of anonymized 48-pixel atlas proxies. Proxy appearance can support neutral visual and spatial distinctions, but biological meaning cannot be assigned and slide-associated acquisition or color effects cannot be excluded.

candidates.qualitative_notes: C0 and C1 provide two broad cellular appearances, but C2 combines nearly empty/background tiles, partial section edges, and pale tissue-containing low-cellularity tiles in its centroids and per-slide examples. The C2 spatial label covers both thin outer boundaries and sizable internal pale regions. C0 occurs on Slides A-E and C1 occurs on A-H, so a coarse recurring cellular contrast is retained, but the required background-versus-pale-tissue distinction is absent. Strong internal separation and coherence (silhouette 0.234, margin q10 0.124, spatial agreement 0.909) do not resolve that visual undersegmentation.

The main K=3 lineages persist and C2 adds a cellular fine state (n=1257) with a coherent region on Slide H and smaller representation on several other slides. However, C3 still spans nearly empty/background, partial-edge, and visibly tissue-containing pale examples across centroid, per-slide, and mid/random views. Low-margin examples also overlap the cellular boundary. Spatial agreement remains high (0.912) and margins are the strongest among the candidates (q10 0.144), but the specified low-content distinction is still not preserved.

C0-C3 retain several cellular-to-transitional appearances, including C2 across all Slides A-H, and the heatmaps show corresponding broad regions. Nevertheless, C4 remains a mixed low-content class: its high-confidence centroids and per-slide examples include both almost empty/outer-edge fields and pale fields with definite tissue content. Thus no clean background/section-edge class is separated from pale low-cellularity tissue. The low-margin overlap is compounded by weak reproducibility for this solution (seed ARI q10 0.525 and LOO minimum ARI 0.508), so the added split does not satisfy qualitative preservation.

This is the first candidate with an unequivocal near-empty/background class, C5 (n=1141), whose centroids and per-slide examples are almost uniformly blank and whose heatmap contribution is mainly a thin outer rim. Pale, low-cellularity but tissue-containing fields remain separately represented by C4 (n=4515) across Slides A-H and occupy wider peripheral or internal regions. Cellular variation is retained by C0 and C1 across Slides A-E and A-D, respectively, by C2 across A-H, and by C3 across six slides; centroid, mid/random, and low-margin views support plausible transitions. The C0/C1 mosaic on Slides A-D indicates a fine cellular split rather than a new macroregion. Margins and spatial compactness are lower than at K=3-4 (margin q10 0.055; 8.60 components per 100 tiles), but the required neutral macro-phenotypes are preserved.

C6 remains a distinct near-empty/background and outermost-edge proxy class across Slides A-H, while C5 retains pale low-cellularity fields as a separate, visibly tissue-containing class. Recurrent cellular appearances remain represented: C3 is seen on A-H, C2 on seven slides, C4 on six slides, and the denser C0/C1 states recur across five and four slides. The extra division relative to K=6 mainly refines cellular or boundary variation and need not denote a new macroregion. Heatmaps retain broad regions but show more fine mosaic structure; margin q10 is 0.046, spatial agreement is 0.730, and fragmentation rises to 9.62 components per 100 tiles.

C7 is an independently recognizable near-empty/background and outermost-edge proxy class, C6 retains pale low-cellularity tissue across A-H, and the small C5 class (n=659) further isolates a very pale but tissue-containing appearance on seven slides. Cellular states remain recurrent through C3 on A-H, C2 on seven slides, and C4 on six slides, with denser C0/C1 recurring across Slides A-E and A-D. Centroid and per-slide exemplars support these distinctions, while low-margin examples show expected boundary mixing. Spatial maps are increasingly fine-grained rather than revealing a necessary new macroregion (margin q10 0.050; spatial agreement 0.727; 9.72 components per 100 tiles).

C8 remains a separate near-empty/background and outermost-edge proxy class across Slides A-H; C7 represents pale low-cellularity tissue; and C6 adds a very pale tissue-containing state on seven slides. Cross-slide cellular variation is still preserved by C4 on A-H, C3 on six slides, and C5 on six slides, while C0-C2 subdivide the denser appearance largely within Slides A-D. The A-D heatmaps show pronounced three-way cellular mosaics, so these are fine states rather than distinct macroregions. This candidate preserves the required types but is the least parsimonious visually and has the weakest separation/compactness profile (silhouette 0.181, margin q10 0.045, spatial agreement 0.713, and 11.05 components per 100 tiles).
